aria: Animated recap of the Pacers' 125 to 120 home win over the Thunder: Pascal Siakam's 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds left that made it 123 to 119, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Siakam's 20 points, the top scorers, how the Pacers won, and the next game.

loser_top: off the bench · 4 of 6 from three
notes: Final score and quarter scores (Thunder 27–24–40–29, Pacers 27–29–40–29; 56–51 Pacers at the half) from the Yahoo Sports and FOX Sports box score pages; the halftime score is also in the AP and VAVEL. The Thunder's full box (120 points, 44 of 101, 13 of 37 from three, 19 of 21 FT, 21 assists, 5 turnovers) is from the Yahoo box score, and its player points add up to 120. A full Pacers player table could not be opened this morning (the Covers and CBS pages were blocked and Yahoo showed only the Thunder table), so the Pacers lines come from written accounts: Siakam 20 (AP, Field Level Media, SI; 9 of 18 and 8 rebounds per FOX Sports, 5 assists per Thunder Wire), Oubre 20, a season high, with 4 of 7 from three (AP, SI, IndyStar), Toppin 17 with 6 rebounds (AP, SI), Slawson 16 with 10 rebounds and 4 blocks (AP, SI, FOX Sports), Nembhard 15 with 6 assists and 11 in the fourth (AP, SI), Zubac 14 with 15 rebounds (AP, Field Level Media, SI, The Oklahoman). Those six account for 102 of the 125; Thunder Wire says six Pacers scored in double figures and SI says a seventh added nine, so the five shown are the top five scorers. The other 23 points are not itemized in the sources read.

Pacers team numbers: 15 of 37 from three (AP, Field Level Media, SI, IndyStar), 12 of 15 FT and 30 assists on 49 baskets (Thunder Wire); 49 baskets, 15 threes and 12 free throws add up to 125. Three-point percentages (40.5% to 35.1%) from Field Level Media, shown rounded. The Pacers' 13-point lead early in the third and the Thunder's 7-point lead in the opening minutes are from Field Level Media. Indiana snapped a four-game losing streak (AP, Field Level Media) and played without Tyrese Haliburton (strained left hamstring, 14th straight game missed, AP). Gilgeous-Alexander scored 38 on 13 of 30 (box score; The Oklahoman; SI). Next: the Pacers host Philadelphia on Friday in an NBA Cup game (AP; SI); the Thunder host Minnesota on Wednesday (AP; The Oklahoman). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Pascal Siakam's 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds left that made it 123–119: AP: Siakam hit "a 3 to give Indiana a 123-119 with 44.4 seconds left"; Field Level Media and Thunder Wire put it at about 45 seconds, and Thunder Wire describes it as a left-wing jumper off Andrew Nembhard's kick-out, with the Thunder down one with 59 seconds left. So the board's Pacers +1 to +4 is 120–119 to 123–119. Oubre then blocked Ajay Mitchell's layup try (AP; Field Level Media) and Zubac dunked off a Nembhard pass with 7.4 seconds left to seal it (IndyStar; Field Level Media). The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Indiana Pacers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Siakam's listed 6-foot-8 and 245 pounds (RealGM), with arms at the default length because no wingspan is reported there, in the Pacers' home kit with No. 43 (RealGM) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
